issues.body: `assert_report_seam` still applies `shlex.split` to the entire `run:` body, finds the script token, requires only that its preceding token is `python3`, and constrains only tokens after the script. Consequently `set -euo pipefail\ntrue || python3 scripts/gate-staleness.py --head-sha "$PR_HEAD_SHA" --base-ref "$PR_BASE_REF"` satisfies the current assertions while `true ||` prevents the reporter from running. `report_mutants()` still tests YAML `if: false` but has no non-crashing shell-level inert mutant. Because the command always exits zero by design, this seam is the claimed defense against a silently absent advisory, and it remains bypassable.
issues.fix_hint: Require the run body to consist of the exact executable command structure (for example, exactly two nonblank lines: exact `set -euo pipefail` and the exact `python3 ...` invocation), or explicitly parse and reject shell control operators/prefixes. Add a mutant using `true || <invocation>` and assert that `assert_report_seam` refuses it.
issues.title: Workflow seam still accepts a conditionally inert shell invocation

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-1 major finding remains unchanged. `assert_report_seam` still tokenizes the whole shell body, locates the script token, and validates only its immediate interpreter and following argv. It therefore still accepts a non-crashing shell prefix such as `true || python3 scripts/gate-staleness.py ...`, which prevents this always-zero advisory from executing. The mutant table still has no shell-level conditionally inert case. The parent-selection, operand validation, reporting, and live workflow wiring otherwise appear coherent, but the advertised structural non-vacuity control is not sound.
